58:1: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: God has heard, O Muhammad, the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband. The one who was arguing with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, concerning her husband was a woman from the Ansar. Scholars differed about her lineage and name. Some of them said: Khawlah bint Tha’laba, and some of them said: Her name is Khawlah bint Tha’laba. Others said: She is Khuwayla bint Khuwaylid. Others said: Khuwayla bint al-Samit. Others said: She is Khuwayla bint al-Dulaij. She used to argue with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about her husband, and her husband was Aws ibn al-Samit. She used to consult him about his matter, and what he said to her: You are to me like my mother’s back, and she used to debate him about that. This is what the people of interpretation said, and the narrations agreed upon it. Mention of who said that, and the traces that came with it: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated: Abd al-A’la narrated: Dawud narrated: I heard Abu al-A’la say: “Khuwayla bint al-Dulaij came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, while Aisha was washing one side of his head. She said: ‘O Messenger of God, my companionship with my husband has been prolonged, and I have become pregnant with him, and he has divorced me.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I am forbidden to him.’ She said: ‘I complain to God of my poverty.’ Then she said: ‘O Messenger of God, my companionship has been prolonged, and I have become pregnant with him.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I am forbidden to him.’ When he said to her: ‘I am forbidden to him,’ she cried out and said: ‘I complain to God of my poverty.’ Then the revelation came down while Aisha was washing the other side of his head. Aisha signaled to her to be quiet. She said: Whenever the revelation came down to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, it would overtake him like a deep sleep. When the revelation had ended, he said: ‘Claim your husband.’ The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to him: ‘God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband.’” And complain to God, and God hears your dialogue.” To His saying: And those who swear off their wives and then go back on what they said (Al-Mujadilah 75:3), that is, go back on it. Then free a slave before they touch each other (Al-Mujadilah 75:3). Can you free a slave? He said: No. He said: But whoever cannot find [a slave], then a fast for two consecutive months (Al-Mujadilah 75:4). He said: O Messenger of God, if I do not eat three times a day, I fear that my sight will go blind. He said: But whoever cannot find [a slave], then feed sixty poor persons (Al-Mujadilah 75:4). He said: Can you feed sixty poor persons? He said: No, O Messenger of God, unless you help me. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, helped him and he fed. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us on the authority of Qatada, he said: It was mentioned to us that Khawlah bint Tha’labah, whose husband Aws ibn as-Samit had divorced her, came complaining to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My husband divorced me when I became old and my bones became weak. So God revealed about her what you hear: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. So he recited until he reached: “He is Pardoning and Forgiving. And those who swear off their wives and then go back on what they said,” wanting to faint after saying that, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: Can you free a freedman? He said: I have no hands for that, or he said: I do not have any. He said: Can you fast for two consecutive months? He said: No, by God, for if he misses food every day repeatedly, his sight will fail. He said: Can you feed sixty poor people? He said: No, by God, unless you help me with your help and prayer. Bishr said: Yazid said: meaning prayer. So he helped him. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him fifteen sa’s, so God collected it for him, and God is Forgiving and Merciful. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Sa’id told us, “On the authority of Qatada, regarding the statement of God, ‘God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. And God hears your dialogue,’ he said: That was Aws ibn as-Samit, declaring divorce from his wife Khuwaylah, daughter of Tha’labah. She said: O Messenger of God, my age has grown old, my bones have become weak, and my husband has declared divorce from me. So God revealed, ‘Those who declare divorce from their wives,’ until His statement, ‘Then go back on what they said,’ (al-Mujadilah 75:3). He meant to say after His statement, ‘Then free a slave before they touch each other.’ So the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him to him and said: ‘Are you able to free a slave?’ He said: ‘No.’ He said: ‘Are you able to fast for two consecutive months?’ He said: ‘If he misses eating three times a day, his sight will go blind.’ He said: ‘Are you able to feed sixty poor people?’ He said: ‘No, unless the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, helps me with it by support and prayer.’ So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, helped him with five.” Ten Sa', and God will gather his affair for him, and God is Forgiving and Merciful." Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ubaydullah bin Musa narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hamza, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: When a man said to his wife in the pre-Islamic era, You are to me like the back of my mother, she would be forbidden to him in Islam. The first to pronounce zihar in Islam was Aws bin as-Samit, who was married to Umar’s daughter, whose name was Khuwaylid, and he pronounced zihar from her. He was disappointed and said, I see that you are forbidden to me, and she said the same to him. He said, “Then go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace.” So she went to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and found a hairdresser combing his hair. She told him, and he said, O Khuwaylid, we have not been commanded to do anything about your matter. So God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he said, O Khuwaylid, be of good cheer. She said, Good. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, recited to her, God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God, up to His saying, Then the freeing of a slave before they touch each other. (Al-Mujadilah 75:3) She said, And what slave is that for us? By God, he cannot find a slave except me. He said, But whoever cannot find a slave, then a fast of two consecutive months (Al-Mujadilah: 4). She said, By God, if he drinks three times a day, he will lose his sight. He said, But whoever cannot afford it, then he should feed sixty poor persons (Al-Mujadilah: 4). He said, From where? It is only a meal or something like it. He said, He should feed him half a wasq thirty sa’s, and a wasq a measure of sixty sa’s. He said, Let him feed sixty poor persons and come back to you. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God to His statement: Then feed sixty poor persons. That is because Khawlah bint as-Samit, a woman from the Ansar, had divorced her husband, and he said: You are to me like the back of my mother. So she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: My husband married me while I loved him, until I grew old and entered old age. He said: “You are to me like the back of my mother, so he left me with no one. So if you can find a dispensation for me, O Messenger of God, with which you can revive me and him, then tell me about it.” So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I have not been commanded to do anything about you until now, but return to your house, and if I am commanded to do something, I will not conceal it for you, God willing. So she returned to her house, and God revealed to His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, in the Book her dispensation and the dispensation of her husband: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband to His statement: And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment. “(al-Mujadilah 58:5) So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent for her husband. When he came to him, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: What do you want with the oath that you swore? He said: Is there an expiation for it? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Can you free a slave? He said: Then all my money will be gone. A slave is expensive and I have little money. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Can you fast for two consecutive months? He said: No, by God, were it not for the fact that I eat three times a day because of my eyesight. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Can you feed sixty poor people? He said: No, by God, unless you help me with that with help and prayer. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will help you with fifteen sa’s, and I will pray for blessings for you. So he reconciled between them.” He said: And he stipulated in it the freeing of a slave for whoever is wealthy. Nothing can be expiated for him except the freeing of a slave if he is wealthy before they have intercourse. If he is not wealthy, then he should fast for two consecutive months. Nothing is permissible for him except fasting if he is poor, unless he is unable to do so. If he is unable to do so, then he should feed sixty poor people. All of that is before intercourse. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Ma`shar al-Madani, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ka`b al-Qurazi, who said: “Khawlah bint Tha`labah was married to Aws ibn al-Samit, who was a man with a defect. He said during one of his migrations: ‘You are to me like my mother’s back.’ Then he regretted what he had said, so he said to her: ‘I think you have been forbidden to me.’ She said: ‘Do not say that, for by God, God does not like divorce.’ She said: ‘Go to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him.’ He said: ‘I feel too shy to ask him about this.’ She said: ‘Then let me ask him.’ He said to her: ‘Ask him.’ So she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: ‘O Prophet of God, Aws ibn al-Samit, the father of my children and the dearest of people to me, has said a word which, by the One upon whom the Book was revealed, he did not mention divorce.’ He said: ‘You are to me like my mother’s back.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘I think you have been forbidden to him.’ She said: ‘Do not say that, O Prophet of God, for by God, he did not mention divorce.’ She turned back to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, several times, then she said: O God, today I complain of the severity of my condition and my loneliness, and how hard it is for me to be separated from him. O God, so send down on the tongue of your Prophet, and you did not leave its place until God sent down: “God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God” until he mentioned the expiations. Then the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: Free a slave. He said: I cannot. He said: Fast two consecutive months. He said: I cannot, for I fast one day and it is hard for me. He said: Feed sixty poor people. He said: As for this, then that is fine. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband. He said: It was revealed about a woman whose name was Khawlah. Ikrimah said her name was Khawlah bint Tha’labah and her husband was Aws ibn as-Samit. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, came and she said: Her husband has made her like his mother’s back to him. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I see that you are forbidden to him. He was washing his head at that time. She said: Look, may I be your ransom, O Prophet of God. He said: I see that you are forbidden to him. She said: Look into my matter, O Messenger of God. She began to argue with him, then he turned his head to wash it, so she turned to the other side and said: Look, may God be your ransom, O Prophet of God. The washer said: Stop talking and addressing her, Khawlah. Do you not see the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, drooping as revelation is revealed to him? Then God revealed, God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband, until he reached, Then they return to what they said (Al-Mujadilah: 3). Qatada said: So he forbade her, then he wanted to go back to her and have intercourse with her, Then the freeing of a slave (Al-Mujadilah: 3), until he reached, He is Aware of what you do (Al-Mujadilah: 3). Ayyub said: I think he mentioned it on the authority of Ikrimah, that the man said: O Prophet of God, I do not have a slave. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I will not do more for you. Then God revealed, Fasting for two consecutive months before they touch each other (Al-Mujadilah: 4). He said: By God, O Prophet of God, I cannot fast. If I do not eat such and such a meal a day, I will encounter and encounter. So he began to complain to Him, but He said: I will not do more for you. Then the following was revealed: But whoever is unable to do so, then the feeding of sixty poor persons (Al-Mujadilah: 4). Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, he said: Ibn Abi Nujayh told us, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty, who argues with you concerning her husband, he said: She argues with Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she complains to God when he is old and she is old until her womb is shaken. Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, who disputes with you concerning her husband, he said: Muhammad has divorced her husband and she is complaining to God. Then he mentioned the rest of the hadith in a similar manner. Abdul Warith bin Abdul Samad told us: My father told us: Aban Al-Attar told us: Hisham bin Urwa told us that he wrote to Abdul Malik bin Marwan: You wrote to me asking me about Khuwaylah, the daughter of Aws bin Al-Samit, and she is not the daughter of Aws bin Al-Samit, but she is the wife of Aws, and Aws was a man who had a problem, and when his problem became severe, he would swear allegiance to her, and when his problem went away, he would not say anything about it. So she came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to ask him for a fatwa and complain to God, and God revealed what you heard, and that is their affair. Ibn Bashar narrated: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated: My father narrated: I heard Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrating on the authority of Muammar ibn Abdullah, on the authority of Yusuf ibn Abdullah ibn Salam, who said: Khawlah, the wife of Aws ibn al-Samit, narrated to me: There was something between me and him, meaning her husband. He said: You are to me like my mother’s back. Then he went out to the gathering of his people, then he came back and tried to seduce me. She said: No, by the One in Whose Hand is my soul, until my affair and your affair are brought before the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and he decides what he will do with me and you. He was an old, weak man, so I overcame him as a strong woman overcame a weak man. Then she went out to a neighbor of hers, borrowed her clothes, came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and sat before him. She mentioned his affair to him, and she did not leave until the revelation came down to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Then she said: He is not able to do that. He said: We will help him with that with a farq of dates. She said: I will help him with another farq and feed sixty poor people. Abu Al-Sa’ib narrated: Abu Mu’awiyah narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamim, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Praise be to God, whose hearing encompasses all sounds. A woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, while I was in a corner of the house, complaining about her husband. I could not hear what she was saying. Then God Almighty revealed: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God to the end of the verse. Isa bin Othman Al-Ramli told me: Yahya bin Isa told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Blessed be He whose hearing encompasses all sounds. A woman would whisper to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and I would hear some of her words, while some of them were hidden from me, when God revealed: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband. Yahya bin Ibrahim Al-Mas’udi narrated to me, he said: My father narrated to me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah, on the authority of Urwah bin Az-Zubayr, he said: Aisha said: Blessed be He whose hearing encompasses all things. I hear the words of Khawlah bint Tha’labah, and some of them are hidden from me, as she complains about her husband to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and she says: O Messenger of God, he has consumed my youth and made my stomach swell for him, until I have grown old and my children have ceased to exist, and he has divorced me. O God, I complain to You. He said: I did not stop until Gabriel, peace be upon him, came down with these verses: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband. He said: Her husband is Aws bin As-Samit. Ibn Wakee’ told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Tamim bin Salamah, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aishah, who said: Praise be to God, whose hearing encompasses all sounds. Khawlah complains about her husband to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and sometimes some of what she says is hidden from me. She said: Then God Almighty revealed: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband and directs a complaint to God. Al-Rabi’ bin Sulaiman told us: Asad bin Musa told us: Hammad bin Salamah told us, on the authority of Hisham bin Urwah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that Jamila was the wife of Aws bin al-Samit, and he was a man who had a severe case of zihar. When his case became severe, he would pronounce zihar on his wife, so God Almighty revealed the verse of zihar. Yahya bin Bishr Al-Qarqasani told me: Abdul Aziz bin Abdul Rahman Al-Umawi told us: Khasif told us, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The zihar of the pre-Islamic era was a divorce. The first person to perform zihar in Islam was Aws bin As-Samit, the brother of Ubadah bin As-Samit, from his Khazrajite wife, Khawlah bint Tha’laba bin Malik. When he performed zihar with her, she thought it was a divorce, so she brought him to the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Messenger of God, Aws has performed zihar with me, and if we separate, we will perish. My belly has been swollen by him, and I have become his companion. She complains about that and cries, but nothing has been revealed about that. Then God, the Almighty, revealed: God has heard the statement of the one who argues with you concerning her husband until His saying: And for the disbelievers is a painful punishment. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called him and said: Do you have the power to free a slave? He said: No, by God, O Messenger of God, I cannot do it. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gathered for him until he freed a slave on his behalf, then he returned to his family. He mentioned that this was in the reading of Abdullah bin Masoud God has heard the statement of the one who is trying to harm you concerning her husband. And His statement: And she complains to God means: And the one who is arguing complains to God about her anxiety due to her husband’s divorce from her, and asks Him for relief. And God hears your dialogue meaning the dialogue between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the one who is arguing is Khawlah bint Tha’labah. Indeed, God is Hearing and Seeing God the Most High says: Indeed, God hears what they respond to and what they converse about, and other than that of the speech of His creation. He is Seeing of what they do and of the work of all of His servants.
58:2: God Almighty says: Those who forbid their women to themselves, God forbids to them the backs of their mothers, so they say to them: You are to us like the backs of our mothers, and that was the way a man divorced his wife in the pre-Islamic era. like that: Yaqub told me: Ibn Ulayyah told us: Ayoub told us, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, who said: Zihar was a divorce in the pre-Islamic era, which if one of them spoke of it, he would never go back on his wife. So God Almighty revealed what He revealed about it. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina except Nafi` read it, and the majority of the reciters of Kufa except `Asim read it asيَتاِرُنوُتwith a fathah on the ya`, a shaddah on the dhaal, and an alif. They also read the other one with the meaning yathaaroon, then the ta` was assimilated into the dhaal, making it a doubled dhaal. It was mentioned that in Abu’s recitation it wasيَتاِرُنوُت and that is to correct and strengthen this recitation. Nafi` and Abu `Amr read it likewise with a fathah on the ya` and a shaddah on the dhaal, except that they read it without an alif:يَتاِرُنوُت. `Asim read it asيَتاِرُنوُتwith a light dhaal, a damma on the ya`, and an alif. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that all of these readings have similar meanings. As for yadhahirun, it is from tadhahir, so it is yatadhahir. As for yadhahirun, it is from tadhahir, so it is yatadhahir. Then the ta’ was assimilated into the dha’, so it was said: yadhahir. As for yadhahirun, it is from zahir yatadhahir. So whichever of these three readings that reciter recites, he is correct. And His statement, They are not their mothers, means that God Almighty says, Their women who swear to divorce their mothers, and say to them, ‘You are to us like the backs of our mothers,’ but rather they are lawful to them. His saying: Their mothers are only those who gave birth to them is not those who said that to them. His saying: And indeed, they say something reprehensible and false. God Almighty says: And indeed, men say something reprehensible and false, meaning lies. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, Abominable speech and falsehood. He said: Falsehood is lying. And indeed, God is Forgiving and Pardoning. God Almighty says: Indeed, God is Forgiving and pardons the sins of His servants if they repent from them and return to Him. He is Forgiving of them that He does not punish them for them after repentance.
58:3: God Almighty says: And those who say to their women, You stink to us like the backs of our mothers. His statement: Then they return to what they said. The scholars differed regarding the meaning of returning to what the one who pronounced shahada said. Some of them said: It is returning to prohibiting what he had prohibited for himself from his wife who was permissible to him before his shahada, so he makes her permissible after he prohibited her for himself by his intention to have intercourse with her and have sexual intercourse with her. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-A’la told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then they return to what they said. He said: He means that he will be overcome after his statement. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, the same. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: Then they return to what they said. He said: He forbade her, then he wanted to return to her and have intercourse with her. Others said something similar to this statement, except that they said: His keeping her after he declared her divorce and not separating from her, is a return from him to what he said, whether he intended to have intercourse or not. Abu Al-Aaliyah used to say: The meaning of his saying: When they said is in what they said. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Abd Al-A’la told us, he said: Dawud told us, he said: I heard Abu Al-A’la say about His statement: Then they will return to what they said: meaning they will return to it. The Arabists differed about the meaning of this. Some of the grammarians of Basra said about this meaning: Freeing a slave before they touch each other, and whoever cannot find one, then fasting, then feeding sixty poor people, then they return to what they said we will not do it and they do it. This is Zihar, he says: She is to me like my mother’s back, and similar words. So if he frees a slave or feeds sixty poor people, he returns to what he said it is forbidden to do, and it is as if the one who said this thought that this is from the introduction which means delay. Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: Then they return to what they said in Arabic is appropriate for: Then they return to what they said, and in what they said, meaning marriage, meaning: they go back on what they said, and in undoing what they said he said: It is permissible in Arabic to say: If he returns to what he did, meaning if he does it again, and it is permissible if he returns to what he did: if he undoes what he did, and it is like you say: He swore that he would hit you, so its meaning is: He swore not to hit you, and he swore to hit you. The correct thing to say about this, in my opinion, is that the meaning of the lam in his statement when they said is in the sense of to or in, because the meaning of the statement is: Then they return to invalidating what they said about prohibiting it and then permitting it. If it is said that its meaning is: Then they return to permitting what they prohibited, or permitting what they prohibited, then that is correct, because all of that is a return to it. So the interpretation of the statement is: Then they return to permitting what they prohibited for themselves from what God permitted for them. His saying: Freeing a slave before they touch each other means: He must free a slave, meaning freeing the slave, male or female, before the man who has made the shahada touches his wife from whom he made the shahada or she touches him. There is a difference of opinion regarding the meaning of touching in this context, similar to their difference of opinion regarding His statement: And if you divorce them before you have touched them (al-Baqarah 2:237), and we have mentioned that there. We will mention some of what we did not mention there. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding His statement, And those who swear an oath of divorce against their wives and then go back on what they said, it is a man who says to his wife, You are to me like the back of my mother. If he says that, it is not permissible for him to approach her by marriage or anything else until he expiates for his oath by freeing a slave. But whoever cannot find [anything] - then a fast of two consecutive months before they touch each other. Touching is marriage. But whoever is not able - then the feeding of sixty poor persons. And if he says to her, You are to me like the back of my mother if she does such and such, then that does not constitute a zihar until he breaks his oath. If he breaks his oath, then he should not approach her until he expiates, and a divorce does not occur in a zihar. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us: Ash’ath told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, that he saw no harm in having intercourse with the woman who had committed li’an without intercourse. Ali bin Sahl told us: Zaid told us: Sufyan said: The only way to refrain from sexual intercourse is to refrain from intercourse. He did not see any harm in relieving himself below the vagina or above the vagina, or wherever he wanted, or to have intercourse. Others said: He meant by that all the meanings of touch, and they said: The verse is general. Who said that? Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Wahib told us, on the authority of Yunus, he said: It was reported to me on the authority of al-Hasan that he disliked touching the woman who pronounces zahar. And His statement: This is what you are admonished by, God Almighty says: Your Lord has made this obligatory upon you as an admonition for you so that you may learn from it, and so that you may refrain from li’an and false speech. And God is All-Aware of what you do, God Almighty says: God is All-Aware of the deeds that you do, O people. Nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for them, so refrain from saying evil and falsehood.
58:4: God Almighty says: And whoever among you who has divorced his wife and cannot find a slave to free, he must fast for two consecutive months before they touch each other. The two consecutive months are those that are not separated by breaking the fast during the day for any of them except for an excuse. If breaking the fast was due to an excuse, then there is a difference of opinion among the scholars. Some of them said: If he broke the fast for an excuse and the excuse is no longer valid, he should continue with the fast he has already done. Others said: Rather, he should start over, because whoever breaks the fast with or without an excuse has not continued fasting for two months. It was mentioned that he said: If he broke his fast due to an excuse and the excuse was removed, he should continue and he is considered a follower. Ibn Bashar told us: Ibn Abi Uday and Abd al-A’la told us, on the authority of Sa’id, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, that he said about a man who fasted as an expiation for zihar, or as an expiation for murder, and became ill and broke his fast, or broke his fast for an excuse, he said: He must make up a day in place of another day, and he does not repeat his fast. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, similarly. Ibn Bashar told us: Yahya told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Arubah, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, regarding the one who has to fast for two consecutive months, and he fasted for a month, then broke his fast, he said: He completes what remains. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Ibn Abd Al-A’la told us, on the authority of Saeed, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan and Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, regarding a man who fasted as expiation for zihar for a month or more and then became ill. He said: He should count what he has passed if he has an excuse. Ibn Bashar told us: Salim bin Nuh told us: Umar bin Aamer told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding a man who was obligated to fast because of murder, a vow, or a slander, and he fasted some of it and then broke his fast, he said: If he was excused, then he must make it up. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: If he breaks the fast due to an excuse, he completes it, but if it is without an excuse, he starts over. Yaqoub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Hajjaj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: If someone had to fast two consecutive months and he fell ill and broke his fast, he said: He must make up what remains of it. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Jurayj told me, on the authority of Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah and Amr ibn Dinar, regarding a man who breaks his fast on a cloudy day, thinking that night has entered upon him in two consecutive months, that he should not do more than replace it, and he should not start over with another two months. Abu Kurayb told me, he said: Ibn Abi Zaydah told us, on the authority of Abd al-Malik, on the authority of Ata’, who said: If a person in seclusion has sexual intercourse and there are still days left of his seclusion, he should complete what remains, and the same applies to the one who has sworn to divorce. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Ata’, he said: If it was something that he was afflicted with, he should continue his fast, and if it was something that he did, he should start over. Sufyan said: This is its meaning. Abdul Hamid bin Bayan told us: Muhammad bin Yazid told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Amer, regarding a man who was devout and fasted two consecutive months except for two days, then he became ill. He said: He completes what remains. Abu Kuraib told us: Ibn Idris told us: I heard Ismail on the authority of Al-Sha’bi something similar. Abu Kurayb and Yaqub told us: Hisham told us, on the authority of Ismail, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, regarding a man who had to fast for two consecutive months, and he fasted and then became ill and broke his fast. He said: He must make up for it and not start over. It was mentioned that he said: He who broke his fast with or without an excuse must fast again. Ibn Bashar told us: Abd al-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding a man who had to fast two consecutive months and broke his fast. He said: He should start over, and if a woman menstruates and breaks her fast, she must make up for it. Yaqub told me, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, he said: If he falls ill and breaks his fast, he should start over, meaning whoever had to fast two consecutive months and falls ill and breaks his fast. Abu Kurayb told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Jabir, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, he said: He starts over. The more correct of the two opinions in our view is the opinion of the one who says: The one who breaks the fast with an excuse should continue, and the one who breaks the fast without an excuse should continue, because of the consensus of all that if a woman menstruates during her fast for two consecutive months with an excuse, then it is the same, because the breaking of the fast by a menstruating woman due to her menstruation with an excuse was from God, so every excuse that was from God is the same. And His statement: But whoever is unable to fast, then he must feed sixty poor people. God Almighty says: Whoever among them is unable to fast, then he must feed sixty poor people. We have already explained the method of feeding previously, so there is no need to repeat it. And His statement: That is so that you may believe in God and His Messenger, God, the Most High, says: This which I have imposed on those of you who profess divorce, is what I imposed when they were able to free a slave, then I made it easier for them when they were unable to do so by fasting, and when they were not able to fast by feeding others. I only did it so that people would acknowledge the Oneness of God and the message of the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and that they would believe in that, act upon it, and refrain from false speech and lying. And these are the limits set by God, God, the Most High, says: These are the limits that God has set for you, and the obligations that He has made clear to you are the limits of God, so do not transgress them, O people. And for the disbelievers, who deny these limits and other obligations of God that they are from God, is a painful punishment, meaning: a painful punishment.
58:5: God Almighty says: Those who fear God in His limits and His obligations, and they make limits other than His limits, and that is opposition to God and His Messenger. As for Qatada, he used to say in the meaning of that, what: Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger means: they are hostile to God and His Messenger. As for his saying: They were humbled as those before them were humbled, it means: They were enraged and humiliated as those nations before them who opposed God and His Messenger were enraged and humiliated. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: They were humbled as those before them were humbled. They were disgraced as those before them were disgraced. Some scholars of Arabic language say: The meaning of kabtawa is destroyed. Another of them said: He says: Its meaning is that they were enraged and humiliated on the day of the Trench, just as those before them were humiliated, meaning those who fought the prophets before them. His statement: And We have sent down clear signs, means: We have sent down detailed evidence and precise signs that indicate the truths of God’s limits. And His statement: And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment. God Almighty says: And for those who deny the clear verses that We sent down to Our Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those who reject them is a humiliating punishment on the Day of al-Qiyamah 75:meaning humiliation in Hell.
58:6: God Almighty says: “And for the disbelievers is a humiliating punishment on the Day when God will resurrect them all. That is the Day when God will resurrect them all from their graves for the Day of Resurrection. Then God will inform them of what they did. God has counted it for them, and they have forgotten it.” God Almighty says: God has counted what they did, so He counted it for them, recorded it, and preserved it, and those who did it have forgotten it. And God is Witness over all things. He says: And God, may His praise be exalted, is Witness over all things they did and other matters of His creation. That is, He witnesses their work and encompasses it, so nothing of it escapes Him.
58:7: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not looked, O Muhammad, with the eye of your heart and seen that “God knows what is in the heavens and what is on the earth of anything? Nothing, small or great, is hidden from Him. He, the Most High, says: How could the deeds of these disbelievers and their disobedience to their Lord be hidden from someone whose description is like this? Then He, the Most High, described His closeness to His servants and His hearing their private conversations and the conversations that people conceal, speaking to Him secretly among themselves. He said: There are not three who confer privately behind Him but He is the fourth of them He hears their secrets and their private conversations, nothing of their secrets is hidden from Him. And not five but He is the sixth of them He says: And there are not five who confer privately but He is the sixth of them likewise. And not less than that He says: And not less than three and not more than five but He is with them when they confer privately wherever they are He says: In whatever place or location they are. What he meant by his saying: He is their fourth is that he is watching them with his knowledge, and he is on his throne. Abdullah bin Abi Ziyad told me: Nasr bin Maymun Al-Madhrub told me: Bakir bin Maruf told us, on the authority of Muqatil bin Hayyan, on the authority of Ad-Dahhak, regarding His statement: There is no confidential conversation between three until His statement: He is with them. He said: He is above the Throne and His knowledge is with them. “Wherever they are. Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things.” And His statement: Then He will inform them of what they did on the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty says: Then He will inform these quarreling people and others of what they did of deeds that He loves or dislikes on the Day of Resurrection. Indeed, God is Knowing of all things. He says: God is Knowing of their private conversations and their secrets, the secrets of their deeds, and other matters of theirs and the matters of His servants. The reciters differed in their recitation of his statement: There is no secret conversation between three. The reciters of the regions recited it as There is no secret conversation between three with a ya, except for Abu Ja`far al-Qari, who recited it as What is with a ta, and the ya is correct in that, due to the consensus of the evidence on it, and its correctness in Arabic.
58:8: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation from among the Jews then they return God Almighty forbade them from it, and they secretly converse among themselves about sin, aggression, and disobedience to the Messenger. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. It was mentioned by the one who said that: Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement: Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret conversation? He said: The Jews. And His statement: Then they return to what they were forbidden from, God Almighty says: Then they return to what they were forbidden from of secret conversation. And they whisper to one another about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, God Almighty says: And they whisper to one another about what God has forbidden them of indecencies and aggression, and that is contrary to the command of God and disobedience to the Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace. The reciters differed in their reading of His statement, and they whisper. The majority of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufians and Basrans, read it as, and they whisper, on the pattern of they interact. Yahya, Hamza, and Al-A’mash read it as, and they produce, on the pattern of they do. Those who read it as, they whisper, found fault with His statement, If you whisper, and did not say, If you produce. And His statement: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, the Most High says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: And when these people who were forbidden from secret conversation come to you, O Muhammad, whom God, the Most High, described to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, they greet you with a greeting other than the greeting that God made for you, and their greeting with which they greeted him, which God informed that He did not greet him with in what came in the reports, is that they used to say: Death be upon you. Mentioning the narration that was reported about that: Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakee’ narrated: Jarir narrated to us, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Ad-Dahha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: Some Jews came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: Death be upon you, O Abu Al-Qasim. I said: Death be upon you, and may God do this and that to you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Aisha, God does not like obscenity. I said: O Messenger of God, do you not see what they are saying? He said: “Do you not see me responding to them as they say? I say: ‘Upon you.’” This verse was revealed concerning that: “And when they come to you with that with which God has not greeted you and say within themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ Hell is sufficient for them, which they will burn, and wretched is the destination.” Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu Al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, who said: The Jews used to come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: Death be upon you. He would say: Upon you. Aisha said: Death be upon you and the wrath of God. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: God does not love the obscene and the vulgar. She said: “They say: ‘Death be upon you.’ He said: “I say: ‘Upon you.’ Then this verse was revealed: ‘And when they come to you with that with which God has not greeted you,’” He said: “The Jews would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: ‘Death be upon you.’” Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, he said: The Jews would come to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and say: Death be upon you. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, And when they come to you with that with which God has not greeted you, to then wretched is the destination, he said: The hypocrites would say to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when they greeted him: Samu alaykum, God said: Hell is sufficient for them; they will burn in it, and wretched is the destination. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, he said: They say, “Say peace be upon you.” He said: They are also Jews. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, They greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, he said: The Jews used to say, Samu alaykum. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, “That Aisha understood what they were saying, so she said: ‘And upon you be death and the curse.’ The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: ‘Take it easy, Aisha, for God loves gentleness in all matters.’ She said: ‘O Prophet of God, have you not heard what they are saying?’ He said: ‘Have you not heard what I say in response to them? I say upon you.’” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik: While the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sitting with his companions, a Jew came to them and greeted them. They responded to him, so the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Do you know what he said? They said: Greetings, O Messenger of God. He said: Rather, he said: Samu alaykum, meaning: You are haraam with your religion. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Did you say: I am haraam with you? He said: Yes. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If one of the People of the Book greets you, then say: Wa alaykum, meaning: Upon you is what you said. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement: And when they come to you, they greet you with that with which God has not greeted you, he said: These are Jews. Three of them came to the door of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and they whispered for a while. Then one of them asked permission, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave him permission. He said: Death be upon you. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Upon you. Then the second, then the third. Ibn Zayd said: Death means death. And the Most High said: And they say to themselves, ‘Why does God not punish us for what we say?’ The Most High said: And those who greet you with this greeting from the Jews say: Why does God not punish us for what we say to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and hasten His punishment for us for that! God says: Hell is sufficient for those who say that, O Muhammad, and it is sufficient for them that they will be exposed to it on the Day of Resurrection. What an evil destination! Hell is that.
58:9: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, “When you confer privately among yourselves, do not confer privately about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger, but confer privately about righteousness meaning obedience to God and that which brings you closer to Him. And piety means: and by fearing Him by performing what He has commanded you of His obligations and avoiding His disobedience. And fear God to whom you will be gathered means: and fear God to whom your return is and with whom you will meet, in neglecting His obligations and advancing in His disobedience, lest He punish you for it when you return to Him.
58:10: God Almighty says: The whispering is only from Satan. Then the people of knowledge differed about the whispering that God said is from Satan, which one is it? Some of them said: What is meant by that is the whispering of the hypocrites to one another. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement: The private conversation is only from Satan to grieve those who believe. The hypocrites were whispering among themselves, and that used to enrage the believers and make them feel heavy, so God revealed about that in the Qur’an: The private conversation is only from Satan to grieve those who believe, but he will not harm them at all. The verse. Others said, including: Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, the Exalted, Indeed, the confidential conversation is only from Satan that he may grieve those who have believed, but he will not harm them at all except by God’s permission, he said: A man would come to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asking him for a need so that the people would see that he had spoken confidentially to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: And the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, would not prevent that from anyone. He said: And at that time the land was at war with the people of this city, and Satan would come to the people and say to them: They are only whispering about matters that have come to pass, and about groups that have been gathered against you and other things, so God said: Indeed, the confidential conversation is only from Satan that he may grieve those who have believed, to the end of the verse. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: When the Muslims saw the hypocrites whispering to each other, it would be difficult for them. Then the verse was revealed: The private conversation is only from Satan, that he may grieve those who believe. Others said: He meant the dreams that a person sees in his sleep that make him sad. Who said that? Ibn Hamid told us: Yahya bin Dawud al-Balkhi told us: Atiyah was asked, while I was listening to the dream, and he said: The dream has three levels. Among them is the whispering of Satan, and that is what He said: Indeed, the secret conversation is only from Satan. Among them is what he talks to himself during the day and sees it at night, and among them is like taking the hand. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: It means the hypocrites’ whispering to one another about sin and aggression. This is because God, the Most High, preceded the prohibition of it with His saying: When you confer privately, do not confer privately about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger. Then He spoke about what is disliked by the people of faith in that, and about the reason for His prohibition of it, saying: “Peace be upon you, secret counsel is only from Satan to grieve those who have believed.” Thus He made clear that since the prohibition of seeing a person in his sleep was like that, and it followed His prohibition of secret counsel because it is from the description of what He prohibited. And His statement, And it will not harm them at all except by God’s permission, God Almighty says: And whispering will not harm the believers at all except by God’s permission, meaning by God’s decree and predestination. And His statement, And upon God let the believers put their trust, God Almighty says: And upon God let the people of faith put their trust in their affairs, and let them not be saddened by the secret conversations of the hypocrites and those who plot against them, for their secret conversations will not harm them if their Lord protects them.
58:11: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, When you are told to make room in assemblies, meaning by His saying make room, make room, from their saying a spacious place if it is wide. The interpreters differed regarding the council in which God commanded the believers to make room. Some of them said: That was the council of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, specifically. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement make room in the assembly, he said: The assembly of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was said to be that in particular. Al-Harith told us, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement O you who have believed, when you are told to make room in the assembly, when they saw someone coming to them, they were reluctant to sit with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he commanded them to make room for one another. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd told us: I heard Ad-Dahhak say, regarding His statement When it is said to you, Make room in the assembly, he said: This was specifically for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and those around him. He said: Make room until every man among you has a seat with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. These are also places for fighting. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement: Make room in the assembly, he said: The women were competing to be in the assembly of the Prophet, so it was said to them: If you are told to make room in the assembly, then make room. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, When you are told, ‘Make room in assemblies,’ then make room; God will make room for you, he said: This was the assembly of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. A man would come and say, Make room for me, may God have mercy on you, and everyone would be content with his closeness to the Messenger of God, so God commanded them to do that, and He saw that it was best for them. Others said: Rather, he meant by that in battle councils when they lined up for war. Mention of the one who said that: Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his saying O you who have believed, when you are told to make room in the assembly, then make room; God will make room for you he said: That is in the assembly of battle. The correct thing to say about this is that God Almighty commanded the believers to make room in the assembly, and He did not specify the assembly of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, for fighting. Both places are called an assembly, so this applies to all the assemblies of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the assemblies of fighting. The reciters differed in their reading of this. The majority of the reciters of the regions read it tafashu fi al-majlis in the singular form, except for al-Hasan al-Basri and Asim, as they both read it fi al-majlis in the collective form, and in the singular form this is the reading according to us, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. And His statement, So make room, means: So make room. God will make room for you, means: God will expand your homes in Paradise. And when it is said to you, ‘Rise,’ then rise, God Almighty says: And when it is said, rise up. What is meant by that is, and when it is said to you, rise to fight the enemy, or to pray, or to do good, or to disperse from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then rise. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, And when it is said, ‘Rise up,’ then rise up to And God is All-Knowing of what you do, he said: When it is said, Rise up, then rise up to goodness and prayer. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then rise up, he said: To every good, fighting an enemy, or enjoining what is right, or whatever is right. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And when it is said, ‘Rise,’ then rise, meaning: If you are called to do something good, then respond. Al-Hasan said: All of this is about conquest. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement: And when it is said, ‘Rise,’ then rise, that when the call to prayer was made, men would become sluggish, so God commanded them when the call to prayer was made to rise to it, to stand up for it. Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And when it is said to you, ‘Rise,’ then rise, he said: Rise from the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. He said: This one is in his house. When it is said to you, ‘Rise,’ then rise from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, because he has needs. So every man of them wanted his last covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to be this. So he said, When it is said to you, ‘Rise,’ then rise. I chose the interpretation that I said about that, because God Almighty commanded the believers, when they are told to rise up, to rise up. Thus, this command encompasses all the meanings of rising up from good deeds, and it is general, so that it is specific to what must be accepted. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina recited it as fanashzu with a damma on the shin, while the majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra recited it with a kasra on it. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings and two famous dialects, like ya’kifūn and ya’kifūn, and ya’rashūn. So whichever of the two readings the reader recites, he is correct. And His statement: God will raise those who have believed among you and those who have been given knowledge, by degrees. God Almighty says: He will raise the believers among you, O people, by their obedience to their Lord in what He has commanded them to do, such as making room in the assembly when they are told to make room, or by their disobedience to good deeds when they are told to go to them. And God will raise those among the people of faith who have been given knowledge by virtue of their knowledge, by degrees above the believers who have not been given knowledge, if they act according to what they are commanded to do. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, God will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees, knowledge has merit for its people, and it has a right over its people, and by my life, the right to you, O scholar, has merit, and God gives every person of merit His merit. Mutraf bin Abdullah bin Al-Shakheer used to say: The virtue of knowledge is more beloved to me than the virtue of worship, and the best of your religion is piety. Abdullah ibn Mutraf used to say: You may meet two men, one of whom fasts, prays, and gives charity more, and the other is far better than him. He was asked: How is that? He said: He is the one who is more pious to God and refrains from what He has forbidden. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement: God will raise those who have believed among you and those who were given knowledge, by degrees in their religion if they do what they are commanded to do. And His statement, And God is All-Aware of what you do, means, the Most High, the Majestic, says: God is All-Aware of your deeds, O people. Nothing is hidden from Him, whether the one among you who obeys his Lord or the one who disobeys Him. He will reward all of you for your deeds, the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for what is due to him, or He will pardon.
58:12: God Almighty says: O you who have believed in God and His Messenger, when you confer privately with the Messenger of God, then give charity before your private conversation to the poor and needy. That is better for you. He says: And giving charity before your private conversation with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is better for you in the sight of God and purer for your hearts from sins. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then present before your private conversation an act of charity, he said: They were forbidden from private conversation with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they gave charity, and no one privately spoke with him except Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. He presented a dinar and gave it in charity, then the permission for that was revealed. Muhammad bin Ubaid bin Muhammad Al-Maharbi told us: Al-Muttalib bin Ziyad told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, who said: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: There is a verse in the Book of God Almighty that no one before me acted upon, and no one will act upon after me: O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity. He said: It was made obligatory, then abrogated. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abu Usamah told us, on the authority of Shibl bin Ibad, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity, he said: They were forbidden from conversing privately with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they gave charity. No one conversed with him except Ali bin Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. He presented a dinar as charity, then the permission was revealed. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, on the authority of Mujahid, saying: Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: There is a verse from the Book of God which no one before me acted upon, and no one will act upon after me. I had a dinar which I exchanged for ten dirhams. Whenever I came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, I would give a dirham in charity. Then it was abrogated, and no one before me acted upon it: O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity. Bishr told us: Yazid told us: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity. He said: The people asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, until they were constantly asking him, so God admonished them with this verse. A man would have a need from the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he would not be able to fulfill it until he presented an act of charity before him, and that would be difficult for them, so God Almighty revealed the concession after that: But if you cannot find [anything], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, he said, Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, When you confer privately with the Messenger, then offer charity before your private conversation. He said: It was abrogated and was only for an hour during the day. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation an act of charity to Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful. He said: The Muslims used to present before their private conversation an act of charity, but when the zakat was revealed, this was abrogated. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, Then offer charity before your private conversations, that is because the Muslims kept asking the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so much so that they became difficult for him. So God wanted to make things easier for His Prophet, so when he said that, many of the people were patient and stopped asking. So after that, God revealed, But if you do not, and God has turned to you in forgiveness, then establish prayer and give zakah, so God made things easy for them and did not make them difficult. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Uthman ibn Abi al-Mughira, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, on the authority of Ali ibn Alqamah al-Anmari, on the authority of Ali, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: What do you think? A dinar? He said: They cannot afford it. He said: Half a dinar? He said: They cannot afford it. He said: What do you think? He said: A barley grain. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You are indeed insignificant. Ali, may God be pleased with him, said: Through me, God made things easier for this nation. And His statement, When you confer privately with the Messenger, then offer charity before your private conversation, then the verse was revealed, Do you fear to offer charity before your private conversation? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, O you who have believed, when you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation some charity, lest the people of falsehood confer privately with the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and that would be difficult for the people of truth. They said: O Messenger of God, we are not able to do that and we are not able to bear it. So God, the Exalted, said, Did you fear to present before your private conversation some charity? So since you did not do it and God has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakah. And He said, There is no good in much of their private conversation, except for those who enjoin charity or righteousness or conciliation between people. (al-Baqarah 2:114), whoever comes to confer with you about this, then accept his private conversation, and whoever comes to confer with you about something other than this, then cut him off and do not confer with him privately. He said: The hypocrites sometimes conferred about things they had no need for, so God, the Exalted, said, Have you not seen those who were forbidden private conversation, then they return to what they were forbidden and confer with one another about sin and aggression and disobedience to the Messenger? (al-Mujadilah 58:8) He said: Because the wicked are included in that. Ibn Hamid narrated: Yahya ibn Wadh narrated to us, on the authority of al-Husayn, on the authority of Yazid, on the authority of Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: He said in al-Mujadilah 58:“When you confer privately with the Messenger, present before your private conversation a charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you cannot find [anything], then indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful.” Then the verse that came after it abrogated it, and He said: “Did you fear to present before your private conversation a charity? But since you did not do it and God has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakah and obey God and His Messenger. And God is Acquainted with what you do.” And His statement, If you do not find anything, God Almighty says: If you do not find anything to give in charity before your private conversation with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, then God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: God is Forgiving of your sins if you repent from them, and Merciful to you that He does not punish you for them after your repentance, and He will not hold you accountable for your private conversation with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, before you give charity before your private conversation with him.
58:13: God Almighty says: It is difficult for you, and you fear, O believers, to offer before your secret conversation with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, the charity of need. The root of the word ishfaq in Arabic speech is fear and caution, and its meaning in this context is: you feared need and poverty by offering charity. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said in interpreting that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Did you fear? He said: Was it difficult for you to give charity? It has been waived for you. And they were commanded to confide in the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, without giving charity when that was difficult for them. Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi told me: Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Shibl bin Ibad Al-Makki, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, the same. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Did you fear to offer alms before your private conversation? But since you did not and God has forgiven you, then establish prayer and give zakat. Two obligatory duties from which no one can return, so this verse abrogated what came before it regarding the command to give alms during private conversation. And His statement: But if you do not do so, and God has forgiven you, God Almighty says: But if you do not offer charity before your private conversations, and God has granted you repentance for your neglect of that, then perform the obligations of God that He has made obligatory upon you and has not removed from you, such as prayer and zakat, and obey God and His Messenger in what He has commanded you to do and in what He has forbidden you to do. And God is All-Knowing of what you do. God Almighty says: God is All-Knowing of your deeds, and He is keeping track of them for you in order to reward you for them.
58:14: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: Did you not look with the eye of your heart, O Muhammad, and see the people who supported a people with whom God was angry, and they are the hypocrites, who supported the Jews and advised them. As Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Have you not seen those who took as allies a people with whom God is angry? to the end of the verse, he said: They are the hypocrites who took as allies the Jews and advised them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada: They took as allies a people with whom God was angry. He said: They are the Jews, whom the hypocrites took as allies. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, the Exalted, Have you not considered those who take as allies a people with whom God has become angry? They are not of you, nor of them, he said: These are the disbelieving Jews among the People of the Scripture, and those who take as allies the hypocrites take as allies the Jews. And he recited the statement of God, Have you not considered those who are hypocrites who say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture (al-Hashr 59:11), until he reached And God bears witness that they are liars (al-Hashr 59:11). If that is what they do not do, and he said: These hypocrites said: We will not let our allies and allies be together for our support and glory, and whoever defends us, we fear that a calamity will befall us. So God, the Exalted, said: Perhaps God will bring about a victory or a decision from Him (al-Ma’idah 59:52), until he reached in their hearts from God (al-Hashr 59:13), and he recited until he reached or from behind walls (al-Hashr 59:14). He said: They do not come out. And His statement, They are not of you, means that the Most High says: These who have taken sides with these people with whom God is angry are not of you, meaning: from the people of your religion and your nation, nor are they of them, nor are they of the Jews with whom God is angry. Rather, He, the Most High, described them as being of you because they are hypocrites. When they meet the Jews, they say, We are with you; we were only mocking. And when they meet those who believe, they say, We believe. (al-Baqarah 2:14) And His statement, And they swear to a lie while they know, God Almighty says: And they swear to a lie, and that is their saying to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: We bear witness that you are the Messenger of God, and they are liars, not believing in him, nor having faith in him, as God Almighty said: And God bears witness that the hypocrites are liars (al-Munafiqun 63:1). It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed about a man from among them whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, rebuked for something that he had heard about him, so he swore a lie. Mention of the report that was narrated about that: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: He said: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: He said: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Sa`id bin Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, who said: “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: A man will enter upon you who looks with the eye of a devil, or with the eye of a devil. Then a blue-eyed man entered, and he said to him: Why do you curse me or insult me? He said: So he began to swear. Then this verse was revealed in al-Mujadilah 58:‘And they swear to a lie while they know it,’ and the other verse.
58:15: God Almighty says: God has prepared for these hypocrites who took the Jews as allies a severe punishment in the Hereafter. Evil indeed is what they used to do in this world by deceiving the Muslims and advising their enemies among the Jews.
58:16: And His statement: They took their oaths as a shield. God Almighty says: They made their oaths and their oaths a shield by which they would protect themselves from being killed and by which they would defend themselves, their wealth, and their children. This is because if hypocrisy is discovered in them, they will swear to the believers in God that they are from them. So they averted [people] from the path of God. God Almighty says: They averted the believers from the path of God with them by their oaths, which they took as a shield, from the path of God with them. This is because they are disbelievers, and God's judgment and His path with regard to the disbelievers among the People of the Book is to kill them or take the jizya, and with regard to the idol worshippers, it is to kill them. So the hypocrites avert the believers from the path of God with regard to them by their oaths that they are believers and that they are from them. Thus, they stand between them and being killed, and they refrain from what the people of faith in God refrain from. His saying, For them is a humiliating punishment, means: For them is a humiliating punishment in the Fire.
